discussion_comments.comment_body: a lot of times this map based merge cause JSON key ordering to change - and that will impact caching of the prompts. do we have any other way to achieve this?

I updated the merge logic to apply keys in deterministic order (sorting base and fallback keys before inserting into the merged map) so the resulting JSON serialization remains stable and doesn't affect prompt caching.

The existing code follows the established pattern in this file: `removeVertexClient` is called on HTTP 401/403 responses (line 1574), not on local token-acquisition errors. Every other method in vertex.go uses the same approach — token errors bubble up as `BifrostOperationError` without evicting the cache; the cache eviction is triggered by the downstream 401/403 response from the Vertex API. The embedding path is consistent with that convention.

Addressed and clarified in d187fb6ff. The path-only key is intentionally a provider-lifetime configuration snapshot: it avoids request-path file I/O and preserves the fasthttp connection pool. Replacing TLS material at the same path takes effect after provider configuration reload (which rebuilds the provider/client); the code naming/comment and GigaChat docs now state this explicitly. Automatic same-path rotation without reload would need an explicit reload/version signal rather than filesystem reads on every request.

Cache-first is intentional and consistent with the rest of governance. The in-memory governance store is the authoritative hot-path source for every auth decision (rate-limit, budget, the LLM gateway) — not just `/mcp` — and it is kept fresh by config sync / propagation. On deactivation, `UpdateVirtualKeyInMemory` updates `IsActive` in place, so the caller's `IsActiveValue()` reads the updated state; on deletion, `DeleteVirtualKeyInMemory` removes the entry, so the by-ID lookup misses and falls through to the config store. The whole point of the cache is to avoid a per-request DB read at request-path scale; reversing the order would defeat it. The staleness window here is identical to the rest of governance, so this is not a new exposure specific to the JWT path.

The signing key is immutable by design — there is no rotation path. `GetOAuth2SigningKey` creates it once via `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` (rdb.go ~L6838), and there is no update/rotate/delete of that row anywhere in the codebase, so the key is identical across nodes and for the process lifetime. JWKS, token issuance, and verification all derive from that same single key, so they cannot diverge. The field doc already records this invariant and notes that the single place to invalidate is here, should rotation ever be introduced — at which point this cache (and only this cache) would need invalidation.
This will break the order of the keys and that has impact on caching - can we somehow remove this?

Thank you for pointing it out, my oversight. The merge path now keeps `output_config` as `schemas.OrderedMap` end-to-end, so key order is preserved and cache-relevant serialization is no longer routed through `map[string]any`

Thanks for pointing this out. I intentionally kept the reconstruction limited to `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, and `total_tokens` because the current list projection does not select `cached_read_tokens`.

So adding `PromptTokensDetails.CachedReadTokens` reconstruction here alone would be misleading: it would work for full DB rows, but not for the actual list-query path this fix targets, where `CachedReadTokens` is still zero because it was not selected.

This PR is scoped to restoring the Tokens column summary in the log list without hydrating S3 payloads. If we want cache-token details in list responses as well, we should make that an explicit follow-up by adding `cached_read_tokens` to `listSelectColumns()` and then reconstructing `PromptTokensDetails` from it with test coverage.
